title: v1/chat.completions compatibility: param orchestrator, weighted-stop dedupe, stream resilience, structured JSON envelope
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a compatibility layer that maps /v1/chat.completions params to Redwood's runtime, stabilizes streaming boundaries, introduces a deterministic preflight for function/tool selection, normalizes logprobs payloads, and emits a compact framed JSON envelope for structured outputs. Backwards-compatible for existing clients; opt-in behavior for framed JSON via response_mode parameter.
description: Context & motivation: Customers integrating with OpenAI /v1/chat.completions expect predictable parity for a) parameter semantics (temperature/top_p/n), b) role and stop handling, c) function/tool calling determinism, d) streaming stability and e) structured output formats. This PR implements a lightweight 'param orchestrator' plus stream resilience and a compact framed-json envelope to reduce client parsing ambiguity. Design highlights: - Param orchestrator: canonicalizes v1 params into our internal runtime hints (temperature->sampling_bias, top_p->nucleus_hint, n->parallel_copies), enforces safe ranges, and emits warnings for ambiguous combinations. - Stop handling: supports both legacy stop arrays and a new weighted-stop list (token + weight). The orchestrator deduplicates equivalent stop sequences, orders stable by token hash, and implements a stop-short-circuit that avoids duplicate fragments in streaming mode. - Streaming stability: introduces a fragment sentinel boundary (\u241E) paired with a heartbeat ping when fragmentization is long-lived; backpressure heuristics reduce jitter seen in high-concurrency workloads. - Function/tool calling deterministic preflight: a lightweight intent-scoring preflight runs in the coordinator so model responses that indicate tool invocation are matched to the highest-confidence registered tool deterministically to avoid flakiness in canary and multiprocess setups. - Structured output: adds an opt-in 'framed_json' response_mode that wraps model output in a small envelope {"frame_v":1, "payload_type":"assistant_response|tool_call|eval", "body":...}. This reduces ambiguity when streaming toolcall metadata and logprob arrays. - Logprobs normalization: canonicalize top_logprobs to a list-of-maps structure, normalize -Inf/NaN to null, and include a token_index map so downstream clients have stable indexing. Checklist: - [x] Param translation and validation + unit tests - [x] Weighted-stop parsing and dedupe algorithm - [x] Stream sentinel & heartbeat implementation + integration test - [x] Deterministic tool preflight and coordinator changes - [x] Framed JSON envelope + docs example - [x] End-to-end compatibility tests against OpenAI fixtures - [x] SDK guidance updates (python/ts) Rollout plan: staged on internal canary -> dedicated infra -> hosted fleet. Feature gated: framed_json is opt-in via response_mode; orchestrator applied for requests that declare api_version: "v1" to minimize risk. Related: ENG-2147, PM-489, SUP-1123. Links: linear/ENG-2147, api-design-doc (private), docs PR will follow.
commits: 4 commits: 1) add param orchestrator + mapping tables, 2) streaming sentinel + backpressure, 3) deterministic preflight/tool router, 4) framed-json envelope and docs updates
diff_snippet:
--- a/service/api/compat/v1_chat_orchestrator.py
+++ b/service/api/compat/v1_chat_orchestrator.py
@@ -1,6 +1,45 @@
+def translate_v1_params(payload):
+    // canonicalize temperature/top_p/n into sampling hints
+    sampling = {}
+    sampling['temperature'] = clamp(payload.get('temperature', 1.0), 0.0, 2.0)
+    sampling['top_p'] = clamp(payload.get('top_p', 1.0), 0.0, 1.0)
+    sampling['copies'] = max(1, int(payload.get('n', 1)))
+    // emit warnings for conflicting params
+    return sampling
